text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past purchases as continuing interest in broadly related products, with insufficient attention to the specific purpose and current need behind each choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they support a concrete task or complement equipment already reflected in the user's history.",
    "Recommendations align when they continue a specific artist, musical style, or repeated theme that matters in recent choices."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items occupy recommendation slots despite weaker connections to the user's demonstrated tasks or preferred content.",
    "Recommendations assume equipment ownership, compatibility, or specialized project needs that prior interactions do not establish.",
    "Recent purchases sometimes trigger redundant replacements or overlapping alternatives despite evidence that the underlying need is already met."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category, ecosystem, and product-family associations substitute for a specific reason to choose an item.",
    "Occasional purchases and superficial similarities, such as shared terminology or compilation titles, receive more weight than sustained preferences."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Repeated and recent interactions jointly identify narrower tasks, artists, themes, and listening preferences.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, connectors, equipment requirements, and intended use determine whether a related product is actually useful.",
    "Purchase history can indicate both an opportunity for complementary supplies and a need that has already been satisfied."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Too many top-ranked items offer broad relevance without a concrete, supported reason to choose them now, leaving too few strong task-specific or taste-specific matches.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The share of top-ranked recommendations users identify as choices they would make now, distinguished from items they merely consider related.",
    "The frequency of unsupported equipment assumptions, compatibility mismatches, and redundant purchases among top-ranked items.",
    "The relative ranks of items matching repeated recent interests versus items linked only to broad categories or isolated interactions.",
    "The frequency of recommendations whose fit remains unassessable because available item information does not identify their content or purpose, tracked separately from explicit mismatches."
  ]
}
